title: Lynn Layton Nissan Team of the Week: West Morgan Rebels - NewsBreak
text:
By Josiah Elmore ,
54 minutes ago
TRINITY, Ala. (WHNT) — The West Morgan Rebels took down the Hatton Hornets 23-14 last Friday.
The Rebels have faced adversity both on and off the field, but still rallied to continue their 29-game regular-season win streak. This earned them the Team of the Week award.
“A lot of resilience, we faced a lot of adversity as this years gone on, you know, I think our guys have responded extremely well to the circumstances that’s kind of gone on, and it’s kind of a next man up mentality and I’ve seen a lot of grit and a lot of toughness,” West Morgan Coach Drew Phillips said.
Phillips says the team came into the game against Hatton with their back against the wall, but fought through to pick up the win.
“I felt like our guys showed that we’re a program, not just a good team, and the guys played for each other, they played tough, fast, physical, disciplined, and together, and you know I was very proud of them,” Phillips said.
The lead-up to the game was especially difficult for the team after their teammate Cole Thorn suffered a brain injury in the Rebels’ game against Priceville.
Senior Jacob Johnston says the team relied on its faith to get through the tough week.
“Faith for sure, faith through prayer for sure. You never know how much you have until something hits you and you lose it. You know that was a big part for us. You know, we were standing up really tall and then something happened and we responded with prayer,” Johnston said. “We could’ve easily given up, we could’ve easily become the broken team that people might see us as right now. We chose to respond with the Lord, and He’s really blessed us with that.”
The Rebels have battled through several other injuries throughout the season, and Phillips says they are hoping to get healthy during the bye week.
West Morgan will be back in action against East Lawrence on Oct. 3.
